items.headline: 66°North gives HOKA's hiking shoe an Icelandic makeover
items.caption: The century-old Icelandic outerwear brand's first footwear collab.
body: 66°North began in 1926 making gear for fishermen.
Built for wind, black sand and ice.
How to wear it: with a shell jacket and wool socks.

items.headline: New Balance's 992 in Black/Turtledove
items.caption: A Made in USA pair from Teddy Santis' line.
body: The 992 has barely changed since 2006.
Smart colour blocking keeps it fresh.
How to wear it: grey sweats, navy coat.

items.headline: Plastic shoes have entered their luxury era
items.caption: From '90s jelly sandals to high-fashion weirdness.
body: Plastic shoes have quietly thrived for decades.
Now designers are making them strange and pricey.
How to wear it: one clear shoe, everything else simple.

items.headline: Rivian makes outerwear with Aether
items.caption: The EV maker teams up with L.A.'s performance-meets-polish brand.
body: Design with a purpose, from cars to coats.
Utility first, but sleek.
How to wear it: over a hoodie on cold commutes.

items.headline: How Celine's Michael Rider seized fashion's attention
items.caption: GQ names the quiet DC designer one of its Men of the Year.
body: His last Paris show was a party, not a crush.
Preppy '80s croquet met new-wave dancers.
Style lesson: preppy is back, but loose.

items.headline: Nike brings back the Air Max 97 'Silver Bullet'
items.caption: The classic turns 30 next year and still looks futuristic.
body: Designed by Christian Tresser.
The wavy lines are often linked to bullet trains.
How to wear it: with black tailoring for contrast.

items.headline: The best fits from GQ Men of the Year 2026
items.caption: From Sebastian Stan's Prada three-piece to Peggy Gou's Schiaparelli.
body: Some went all out; others wore their own clothes.
Both approaches worked.
Style lesson: a three-piece suit is a statement.

items.headline: Bond's luggage brand Globe-Trotter breaks its own rules
items.caption: Daniel Craig's 007 travelled with it; now it's trying something new.
body: Over a century making its signature case in Hertfordshire.
Fans include Kate Moss.
Style lesson: buy luggage that ages well.

items.headline: Saman Amel x Mytheresa go Alpine again
items.caption: The tailors swap suits for shearling, down and cashmere.
body: Their second ski-inspired collection.
Made for après-ski and chalet evenings.
How to wear it: shearling over a roll neck.

items.headline: Hublot makes denim permanent in the Big Bang line
items.caption: The statement watch now comes in denim for good.
body: The Big Bang has always been bold.
Denim joins the permanent collection.
Style lesson: match the strap to your jacket.

items.headline: HU-02 revives the Art Deco 'Chronoscope' jump hour
items.caption: A fan-favourite design returns as a disco volante case.
body: A favourite design, brought back.
Hours jump instead of sweeping.
Style lesson: odd shapes suit plain cuffs.

items.headline: Antarctic blue whales grew 1,000% since whaling ended
items.caption: From 418 whales to 4,018, about 4.5% growth a year.
body: Illegal whaling finally stopped in 1973.
They have about one calf every three years.

items.headline: New therapy wipes out deadly brain tumours in every mouse tested
items.caption: UCSF's immune cells switch on only inside the brain.
body: They also blocked new tumours weeks later.
It targets a deadly childhood cancer.

items.headline: Siblings build a 430-step 'sky ladder' for their mother
items.caption: Their mother refused to leave her mountain home in Zhejiang.
body: She once held their hands down the old path.
Now it's their turn.

items.headline: Students fight to save a poached Silicon Valley wildflower
items.caption: The Santa Clara Valley 'liveforever' grows only near their campus.
body: It feeds pollinators.
It's one of California's most poached wild plants.
